title: Remarriage Terms for Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) Surviving Spouses
content:
The following terms apply to a surviving spouse receiving Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) who remarries or lives with another person as a spouse. They do not differ between the six rate categories (DIC Surviving Spouse (Basic Rate), DIC Surviving Spouse (Basic Rate with 8-Year Provision), DIC Surviving Spouse (Housebound), DIC Surviving Spouse (Housebound with 8-Year Provision), DIC Surviving Spouse (Aid and Attendance) and DIC Surviving Spouse (Aid and Attendance with 8-Year Provision)).

| Term | Setting in every rate category |
|---|---|
| Remarriage retention age | 55 — the age at or after which a surviving spouse who remarries keeps DIC |
| Remarriage before the retention age ends DIC | Yes |
| Living with another person and holding out as spouses is treated as remarriage | Yes |
| DIC can be resumed after a disqualifying remarriage ends by death or divorce | Yes |
| When termination for remarriage takes effect | The last day of the month before the remarriage |
| Ages from which remarried surviving spouses keep or may restore DIC | Remarriage at or after age 55 |

### Reading the terms by age at remarriage

| Age of the surviving spouse on the date of remarriage | Remarriage ends DIC? |
|---|---|
| Under 55 | Yes |
| 55 or older | No — DIC is kept |

### Hypothetical illustrations

- A surviving spouse remarries on the day of their 55th birthday. Remarriage at age 55 is at the retention age, so DIC is kept.
- A surviving spouse remarries on the day before their 55th birthday, while still 54. Remarriage before age 55 ends DIC, and the termination takes effect on the last day of the month before the month of the remarriage.
- A surviving spouse aged 50 begins living with another person and the two hold themselves out as spouses. That arrangement is treated as a remarriage before age 55.
